passage:
“Mama! Mama! Manoj took a biscuit before lunch!” Arohi ran into the kitchen, eyes shining.

“Did he?” Mama said, stirring the dal. “How do you know?”

“I saw! Dadi saw too. He hid it under the pillow.”

Manoj appeared at the door, red-faced. “It was only one.”

Mama looked at Arohi. “Thank you for telling me. Did you want a biscuit too?”

Arohi looked at the floor, then up. “I wanted you to say I'm good.”

“You're good either way,” said Mama. “Come and help me with the rotis.”

qa.q: What did Arohi say Manoj took before lunch?
qa.a: Arohi said Manoj took a biscuit before lunch.

qa.q: Why did Arohi run to tell Mama about the biscuit?
qa.a: Arohi was eager for Mama's praise and wanted to hear Arohi is good, so telling was a way of getting approval; the shining eyes show Arohi's excitement.

qa.q: What choice did Mama make that changed the mood in the kitchen?
qa.a: Mama thanked Arohi for telling, asked about Arohi's own wish for a biscuit and said Arohi is good either way.

qa.q: How might Manoj feel standing at the door red-faced?
qa.a: Manoj probably felt embarrassed and caught out, and perhaps annoyed that Arohi told.

grounding: A young child announces who did what to win adult approval and test rules, closer to reporting than malice.

passage:
Teacher's note, Nursery B, Wednesday. During free play Wasim came to me four times in ten minutes. “Jasleen threw a block.” “Ayaan took the red one.” “Jasleen said a bad word.” Each time he studied my face. He wasn't upset. He seemed pleased to have something to tell.

I thanked Wasim for telling me and said I would look when someone was hurt. I asked Jasleen quietly what had happened: a tower had fallen. Then I gave Wasim a job, tidying the red blocks. I'll keep watching whether reporting is how he asks for attention.

qa.q: How many times did Wasim come to the teacher in ten minutes?
qa.a: Wasim came to the teacher four times in ten minutes.

qa.q: What does Wasim studying the teacher's face after each report suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Wasim wants to see whether the news earns approval, and is pleased to have something to tell.

qa.q: What did the teacher do after thanking Wasim?
qa.a: The teacher asked Jasleen quietly what had happened and gave Wasim a job tidying the red blocks.

qa.q: How might Jasleen feel hearing the reports from the block corner?
qa.a: Jasleen might feel embarrassed or worried about getting into trouble, even though a tower had simply fallen.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a young child repeatedly reporting what others did, seeking adult approval, and how the teacher responded.
